Convert HiTOP-DAT Scale Scores to T Scores

Source: R/norm_hitopdat.R
norm_hitopdat.Rd

Converts the scale scores from score_hitopdat() to T scores against the norms the battery's authors named, and flags high IDAS-II Suicidality and CAT-PD Self-Harm T scores. The norms are in hitopdat_norms.

Usage

norm_hitopdat(data, prefix = "dat_", alert_t = 65, append = TRUE)

Arguments

data

A data frame holding the scale score columns that score_hitopdat() returns, named prefix plus each scale's camelCase name in hitopdat_norms. Other columns are ignored. Each score column must be numeric or logical; any other column, such as text or a bit64 integer64 column, is an error of class hitop_nonnumeric_items.

prefix

The prefix of the score column names, and of the columns this function adds. Use the prefix given to score_hitopdat(). Set it to an empty string "" when the columns have no prefix. (default = "dat_")

alert_t

The T score at or above which an alert column is TRUE: one finite number. (default = 65)

append

An optional logical indicating whether the new columns should be added to the end of the data input. (default = TRUE)

Value

A tibble with one _t column per scale in hitopdat_norms order (prefix plus the scale's camelCase name plus "_t"), then the logical columns prefix plus "suicidality_alert" and prefix plus "selfHarm_alert", after all original data columns (if requested).

Details

T scores. Each scale's T score is 50 + 10 * (score - M) / SD, with the scale's M and SD from hitopdat_norms, rounded to a whole number with halves rounded away from zero. Both of the authors' versions of the battery round T scores to whole numbers. A score of NA gives a T score of NA. The norms and their sources are:

  • WHODAS: Andrews et al. (2009), Table 1, the total row and column.

  • The 18 IDAS-II scales: Watson et al. (2012), Table 2, the "Adults" column.

  • CAPE positive symptoms: Galletly et al. (2016), Table 1, the men's and women's means weighted by their n, with the SD printed for both, divided by the 20 items.

  • The 33 CAT-PD facets: the "Community" means and SDs of Len Simms's CAT-PD and IDAS scoring workbook. These norms are unpublished. The battery's authors use them, and this function follows the authors.

The AUDIT, DUDIT and PHQ-15 get no T score. The AUDIT and DUDIT norms are split by sex, and how to report them waits on the authors' answer. The authors keep the PHQ-15 on its cutoff scores rather than a T score. The IDAS-II General Depression scale is not scored (see score_hitopdat()).

Alerts. The battery alerts on two scales: IDAS-II Suicidality and CAT-PD Self-Harm. Each alert column is TRUE when its scale's rounded T score is at least alert_t, FALSE when it is lower, and NA when the T score is NA. The default of 65 is the alert point Katherine Jonas, the battery manual's first author, gave in her email to the package maintainer of 2026-10-15. She added that clinics may set another, for example to suit their state's laws.

Errors. A score column missing from data, or a score column name held by more than one column of data, is an error that names it.

With append = TRUE, a column of data whose name this call would also produce is an error rather than an overwrite or a duplicated column: the message names every colliding column. Re-run with append = FALSE to return only the new columns, or drop the colliding columns from data first. The condition is classed hitop_append_collision, so a caller can catch this refusal by name.

References

Andrews, G., Kemp, A., Sunderland, M., Von Korff, M., & Ustun, T. B. (2009). Normative data for the 12 item WHO Disability Assessment Schedule 2.0. PLoS ONE, 4(12), e8343. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0008343

Galletly, C., Clark, L., McFarlane, A., Searle, A., Sawyer, M., Sim, M., Baghurst, P., & van Hooff, M. (2016). Childhood lead exposure, childhood trauma, substance use and subclinical psychotic experiences: A longitudinal cohort study. Psychiatry Research, 239, 54-61. doi:10.1016/j.psychres.2016.02.066

Simms, L. J. (n.d.). CAT-PD and IDAS scoring [Unpublished Excel workbook]. Received by the package maintainer from K. G. Jonas, 2026-10-15.

Watson, D., O'Hara, M. W., Naragon-Gainey, K., Koffel, E., Chmielewski, M., Kotov, R., Stasik, S. M., & Ruggero, C. J. (2012). Development and validation of new anxiety and bipolar symptom scales for an expanded version of the IDAS (the IDAS-II). Assessment, 19(4), 399-420. doi:10.1177/1073191112449857

See also

score_hitopdat(), hitopdat_norms

Examples

# Five simulated respondents, each answer drawn from its item's answer set
set.seed(1)
answers <- lapply(hitopdat_items$Choice_Set, function(set) {
  values <- hitopdat_choices$Value[hitopdat_choices$Choice_Set == set]
  values[sample.int(length(values), 5, replace = TRUE)]
})
names(answers) <- sprintf("hdat_%03d", hitopdat_items$Item)
scores <- score_hitopdat(as.data.frame(answers), items = names(answers),
                         append = FALSE)
t_scores <- norm_hitopdat(scores, append = FALSE)
t_scores[, c("dat_suicidality_t", "dat_suicidality_alert",
             "dat_selfHarm_t", "dat_selfHarm_alert")]
#> # A tibble: 5 × 4
#>   dat_suicidality_t dat_suicidality_alert dat_selfHarm_t dat_selfHarm_alert
#>               <dbl> <lgl>                          <dbl> <lgl>             
#> 1                83 TRUE                              81 TRUE              
#> 2               130 TRUE                              70 TRUE              
#> 3               104 TRUE                              79 TRUE              
#> 4               100 TRUE                              72 TRUE              
#> 5               109 TRUE                              81 TRUE              

# A clinic that alerts at T 70
norm_hitopdat(scores, alert_t = 70, append = FALSE)$dat_selfHarm_alert
#> [1] TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE
